parameters.content:
## OPS - Capacity Ranker Campaign Watchdog

Every 5 minutes, 08:00–21:00 ET, Mon–Sat: GET LP-MCP `/n8n/capacity-ranker/campaign-state`.

**This workflow does not alert. LP-MCP does.** The route reads both Data campaigns (`Data - Hot Leads less than 7`, `Data - Warm Leads less than 30`) and posts the GroupMe alert itself when either is not RUNNING, suppressed to once per campaign per 30 minutes. `GROUPME_BOT_ID` is set on LP-MCP and on neither n8n service, and n8n runs with `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE` set, so an alert built here posted with no bot id and was rejected silently. The bot id stays on the LP-MCP side.

**Why it exists:** the ranker (`CAPACITY_RANKER_CYCLE_CAMPAIGNS`) stops → reorders → restarts each Data campaign. Its `finally` block guarantees the restart at the process level but cannot cover a crash between stop and start. This is that cover. **Do not enable the cycle flag until this workflow is ACTIVE.**

**Activating this workflow IS the on switch** — nothing else calls the route, so no alert can fire until you turn it on.

**Reading the executions:** a 200 is a healthy floor. Any failed execution means either a campaign is down (503, and LP-MCP has already paged GroupMe) or the check itself could not run (LP-MCP down or unreachable — nobody was paged, so look now).

nodes.name: GET campaign-state
nodes.notes: 200 = both Data campaigns RUNNING. 503 = one is not, and LP-MCP has already sent the GroupMe alert. Errors are deliberately NOT swallowed: a failed execution here is the only signal left if LP-MCP itself is unreachable.

meta.note: Lives in n8n as workflow zIJSpafEg5Gwx2Mw, inactive. Mark activates it before enabling CAPACITY_RANKER_CYCLE_CAMPAIGNS on LP-MCP.
